scamsFlagged.label: Full system, our own cases
scamsFlagged.note: A ceiling: we wrote these cases

scamsFlagged.label: Full system, blind test by someone else
scamsFlagged.note: 50 cases, run once, before the fixes

findings.found: Blind test: scams with tiny notes and small amounts slipped through (4 of 25).
findings.fix: Ask the customer a short question when the evidence is thin, then decide again.

findings.found: A surprise gift ('keep it secret') was treated as concealment and held.
findings.fix: The reader now tells a harmless surprise from real concealment, and the guard asks before it holds.

findings.found: Small-business owners got friction on 43% of normal payments.
findings.fix: Larger payments count for less against a business customer's own habits.

findings.found: Eight payments to one new payee in a day only ever earned a question.
findings.fix: 15 days of history: repeat payments to a new payee, total sent to one payee, and heavy spend all add risk.

findings.found: Hidden orders to the checker, in eight wordings including other languages.
findings.fix: Orders are treated as a warning sign. All eight were held on the first run.

findings.found: A second test file was built from templates: 17 unique notes in 50 cases.
findings.fix: Rejected as a headline test. Replaced by an automatic scenario factory with a simulated customer.

findings.found: Cloud Run swallows the /healthz path, so the health check returned 404.
findings.fix: The tester checks the home page, and the server's own route moved to /api/health.

findings.found: Every answer reveals the risk score and reasons, which could help an attacker tune a message.
findings.fix: Kept for the demo. A production version would send only the action and a warning to the customer.

limits: All data is made up. Nothing here has met real customers or real fraud.
Our own 99% is a ceiling, because we wrote the cases. The blind test is the fairer guide.
Some quiet scams show nothing unusual in the payment itself. Only the customer's words can reveal them, and a coached customer can hide them.
Payee reputation (for example accounts reported by other banks) is not modelled. A real bank would add it.
The prototype runs on the free trial's allowance, with rate limits and a cost guard, so it is not sized for heavy traffic.
